newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian woman refuses release from Israel jail.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian woman refuses release from Israel jail.

text.p: A Palestinian woman convicted of drug offences and due to be released from an Israeli prison has refused to leave jail, Israeli and Palestinian officials said on Thursday.

"She doesn't want to leave," an Israeli prisons spokeswoman said of Zaynab Abu Sido, who was due to be freed along with 30 other Palestinian woman prisoners earlier this week under an Israel-PLO peace deal.
A prisons source who refused to be identified said Abu Sido, from Gaza, feared she would be ostracised or even harmed if forced to return to Palestinian self-rule areas.
Hisham Abdel Razeq, Palestinian Authority chief negotiator on prisoners, confirmed Abu Sido refused to leave jail.
Palestinian human rights lawyer Subhiya Jumaa told Reuters a woman who had served time for drugs crimes could face a harsh life upon being released in conservative Gazan society.
"Under such a conservative community, with certain traditions, it could happen," Jumaa said. "There is fear."

The other 30 Palestinian women prisoners were received by Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and cheering crowds on Wednesday in self-ruled Ramallah. Israel promised to free the women under a 1995 peace deal with the PLO.
Palestinian prisoners negotiator Sufyan Abu Zaydeh told Reuters some 3,000 male prisoners remained in Israeli jails. Israeli sources put the number closer to 2,200.
